justification_text:
The point estimates at each horizon were driven by a combination of recent trends, historical data, and any observable patterns that give insight into near- and medium-term behavior. For the 1-day forecast, I placed the highest weighting on immediate, short-term signals—such as momentum in recent data or seasonality—that suggests the value will remain close to 381.5, reflecting minimal change over such a short horizon. For the 1-week and 1-month forecasts, I incorporated expectations of gradual trends based on past observations, assuming there are no major disruptive events. The slightly upward shift in the estimates over time reflects a projected continuation of the underlying trend or growth pattern, moving incrementally higher as more time passes.

The widening of the confidence intervals at longer horizons reflects increasing uncertainty as time stretches forward. In the short term, uncertainty is lower because fewer factors have the opportunity to significantly influence outcomes. For example, in one day, abrupt or random shifts are less likely unless tied to scheduled events or breaking news. By contrast, over the course of a week or a month, a wider range of variables could come into play, such as unexpected news, market sentiment shifts, or changes in external conditions. This is why the 90% confidence interval grows broader, from just a few points for 1 day to a span of 40 points for 1 month.

There are, however, specific risks and events that could result in outcomes outside of these intervals. These could include unexpected macroeconomic events, sudden geopolitical tensions, or unforeseen shocks to the system—such as major policy announcements, technological disruptions, or natural disasters. Any of these could introduce volatility not accounted for in the historical data or trends that informed these forecasts. Similarly, structural changes in the underlying process could invalidate the assumptions underlying these estimates, pushing outcomes well outside the anticipated range. These risks grow more prominent as the horizon lengthens, adding additional context to the broader confidence intervals at the 1-month mark.
